setup.why: Use pre-existing pool folders to exercise both the has-subfolders and zero-subfolders branches; no write capability available (read-only round).

item_shape.folders[]: id:int, project_id:int, group_id:int, name:string, is_automation:bool, sub_folders_count:int, cases_count:int, total_cases_count:int, links.self:string
item_shape.self: id:int, project_id:int, group_id:int, name:string, parent_id:int|null(absent when self is root? no - present, null observed as top-level parent_id not self.parent_id), notes:string(HTML-escaped, only present when non-empty), is_automation:bool, cases_count:int, total_cases_count:int, sub_folders_count:int, contents[]:same shape as folders[] items but group_id observed as STRING with a DIFFERENT value than the matching folders[] entry, links.self:string
item_shape.info: page:int, page_size:int(fixed 300), count:int, prev:int|null, next:int|null - same 5 keys present on every branch tested (0 subfolders, 7 subfolders); no total_pages key ever observed

notes:
PAGINATION CHECK: exercised both reachable branches — __scratch__/764138 (7 direct subfolders) and __readonly__/764093 (0 subfolders). Both returned the identical info envelope shape declared in the schema: {page, page_size, count, prev, next}, all 5 keys always present, prev/next null in both cases (count 7 and 0 respectively, both far under the fixed page_size=300 ceiling). No total_pages key was ever observed, and no second, prev/next-only shape was seen — this capability does NOT show the two-mutually-exclusive-info-shapes defect found on the sibling capability, at least for single-page results. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the pool's largest folder has only 7 subfolders, far short of the 300-per-page ceiling, so a genuine next-page response (info.next != null) was NOT reachable and the multi-page branch is UNVERIFIED, not confirmed — cannot rule out a shape change once pagination actually kicks in.

CONFIRMED per sibling guidance: `test_cases` is ALWAYS null (observed null on every call: plain, detail=true, nested_sub_folders=true). CONFIRMED: `folders` holds immediate children only (matches `self.contents` for a one-level call; deep folder 764827 under 764828 never appears in the top-level `folders` array of the 764138 call).

DRIFT FOUND (reproduced on all 3 default-mode calls, both pool folders): `self.contents[].group_id` is returned as a STRING (e.g. "3452") whose value DIFFERS from the value in the top-level `folders[].group_id` for the exact same folder object (returned as an INTEGER matching self.group_id, e.g. 2615). The declared schema types group_id as integer for both `folders[]` and `self.contents[]` items (same item schema is reused). So `self.contents[].group_id` violates the declared type (string vs integer) AND appears to carry a stale/wrong group id relative to the folder's actual group (2615, confirmed via self.group_id and folders[].group_id). This is reproducible, not a one-off.

ID TYPE CHECK: unlike get_folder_tree_v1, this capability returns `id` as an integer (not a quoted string) consistently everywhere (folders[], self, self.contents[], nested contents[]), and `parent_id` is also an integer everywhere it appears. No id/parent_id type inconsistency found here — this capability does NOT reproduce that sibling defect.

ADDITIONAL OBSERVATIONS (secondary params, not part of the core default-path verdict but recorded since discovered): (1) detail=true on a root folder (764138, whose own parent_id is null) returned `ancestors: []` (empty array) rather than the documented null-vs-breadcrumb dichotomy being demonstrated with actual ancestor entries — consistent with 'root folder has no ancestors' but not a full confirmation of populated-breadcrumb behavior since no non-root pool folder was available to test with a deep chain from the root. (2) nested_sub_folders=true CONTRADICTS its own guidance: guidance states 'self.contents is stripped from the response' when nested_sub_folders takes effect, but the actual response still included `self.contents`, fully populated and even recursively nested one level deeper (folder 764828's `contents` held its child 764827). (3) On the nested_sub_folders=true call, `info` came back as a bare `null` instead of the declared object — a second, separate contract violation from the group_id one, only present when nested_sub_folders is used (default/plain calls always returned the full info object). (4) On the same nested_sub_folders=true call, `self.cases_count` was 0, contradicting the 18 direct cases confirmed for folder 764138 on every plain call — value changes depending on mode for the identical folder, a real behavioral inconsistency, not just a shape issue. (5) case_count=true / total_count=true (declared as 'read only on nested_sub_folders path') produced no visible additional fields — cases_count was already present regardless, and no per-branch total-count field appeared; their effect could not be positively confirmed. These four nested-mode observations are secondary/bonus findings outside the plain single-level contract this run targeted, but are recorded verbatim since they surfaced during probing. Folder notes are HTML-escaped as documented (__scratch__ notes: '<p>write probes create their own objects in here</p>'); the `notes` key is simply absent (not present as null) on __readonly__/764093, which has no notes set.
